level_1_minor.description: First aid treatment, minor equipment damage, near-miss events requiring investigation but no lost time
examples: Minor equipment malfunction with no safety impact
Small fluid leaks contained at source

level_2_moderate.description: Lost time injury, significant equipment failure, environmental incident, partial evacuation required
level_2_moderate.personnel: Safety manager, first response team, shift supervisor
examples: Conveyor belt fire contained to single section
Small chemical spill within secondary containment

notification_requirements.documentation: MSHA Form 7000-1 within 10 working days, internal incident report within 48 hours

level_3_major.description: Hospitalization of multiple persons, structural failure of primary infrastructure, uncontrolled fire, significant ground failure, serious environmental release
level_3_major.personnel: Emergency response team, mine management, safety department, external emergency services on standby
examples: Roof collapse or rib failure in active workings
Fire extending beyond point of origin
Significant ground failure affecting main access

notification_requirements.documentation: Immediate verbal report to MSHA, written report within 24 hours, MSHA Form 7000-1

level_4_catastrophic.description: Fatality, mine collapse, multiple fatality event, uncontrolled major fire, explosive atmosphere, complete structural failure, mass casualty event
level_4_catastrophic.personnel: Full emergency response deployment, mine management, corporate executive team, federal and state regulators, external emergency services (fire, EMS, SAR, hazmat), media and family liaison
examples: Complete mine collapse or pillar recovery failure
Massive underground fire with smoke propagation throughout workings

notification_requirements.documentation: Immediate verbal notification to MSHA, written report within 15 minutes, comprehensive report within 24 hours, ongoing updates every 4 hours until stabilized

immediate_actions.action: Activate nearest fire alarm pull station and radio emergency channel
Sound underground emergency siren pattern (3 long blasts)
All personnel in affected zone begin self-rescuer donning and evacuation via primary escape way
immediate_actions.responsible: All underground personnel in affected zone

immediate_actions.action: Emergency response team dons firefighting equipment and proceeds to fire location via fresh air base
Supervisor conducts headcount at designated assembly point
Ventilation adjustments to control smoke propagation - consideration of reversing, stopping, or maintaining airflow
immediate_actions.responsible: Ventilation engineer and mine rescue captain

immediate_actions.action: Coordinate with surface emergency response and external fire services
Establish command post and begin incident command system protocols

evacuation_routes.primary_escape_way: Designated escapeway with fresh air supply, marked with luminous directional signs at 50-foot intervals, clear of obstructions, minimum 4.5 feet wide by 6.5 feet high
evacuation_routes.secondary_escape_way: Alternative escapeway through separate ventilation split, accessible if primary is compromised

refuge_chambers.location_requirement: Within 1500 feet of all active working faces per MSHA 30 CFR 75.1704
refuge_chambers.capacity: Minimum 15-minute supply of compressed air, water, and communication to surface
refuge_chambers.duration: 96-hour rated sealed refuge alternatives where applicable
refuge_chambers.inspection: Daily by shift supervisor, weekly by safety department

self_rescuers.location: Within 25 feet of all working positions and at all entry points to underground
self_rescuers.training: Annual refresher per MSHA 48.32, practical donning exercise
self_rescuers.inspection: Daily visual inspection, monthly function test

evacuation_markers.spacing: Every 50 feet along escapeways and at all intersections

portable_extinguishers.placement: Within 50 feet of electrical equipment, within 100 feet of flammable material storage
portable_extinguishers.inspection: Monthly by safety department, annual professional servicing

fixed_suppression.deluge_systems: At belt drive heads, crusher stations, underground workshops
fixed_suppression.sprinkler_systems: In processing plants, warehouses, electrical rooms

fire_fighting_strategy.electrical_fire: De-energize equipment before attempting suppression, use CO2 or dry chemical extinguishers, never use water on energized electrical equipment
fire_fighting_strategy.belt_fire: Activate deluge system if available, apply water spray to cool surrounding structure, remove fuel source if possible, evacuate beltway if fire cannot be controlled within 5 minutes
fire_fighting_strategy.diesel_fire: Use foam or dry chemical, do not use water jet (may spread burning fuel), activate fuel shutoff valves
fire_fighting_strategy.coal_dust_fire: Apply water spray to prevent spread, use rock dust to inert atmosphere, carefully approach with CO monitoring
fire_fighting_strategy.electrical_substation: De-energize remotely, apply CO2 extinguishers, do not enter until confirmed de-energized

mine_rescue_equipment.breathing_apparatus: BG-4 or equivalent closed-circuit breathing apparatus, 4-hour duration
mine_rescue_equipment.gas_detection: Multi-gas detectors (CH4, CO, CO2, O2, H2S), calibrated weekly
mine_rescue_equipment.thermal_protection: Fire-resistant suits rated to 500 degrees F for 30 minutes
mine_rescue_equipment.communication: Through-earth communication systems, leaky feeder, and emergency communication cables

communication_protocols.initial_alarm: Radio emergency channel 1, mine telephone to surface, fire alarm pull station, emergency siren
communication_protocols.status_updates: Every 10 minutes from incident commander to surface command post
communication_protocols.external_notification: Activate 911 dispatch, notify local fire department with mine maps, request mutual aid if multiple companies in area

post_incident_procedures.re_entry_criteria: Atmosphere monitoring confirms safe conditions (CO < 25 ppm, O2 > 19.5%, no flammable gases), structural assessment by qualified engineer, MSHA approval obtained
post_incident_procedures.ventilation_restoration: Gradual return to normal ventilation under controlled monitoring, continuous atmospheric monitoring during restoration
post_incident_procedures.damage_assessment: Engineering assessment of structural damage, equipment condition evaluation, infrastructure integrity verification
post_incident_procedures.evidence_preservation: Photograph and document scene before disturbance, preserve electronic data from monitoring systems, secure equipment involved in incident
post_incident_procedures.return_to_work: All personnel briefed on incident findings, updated safety procedures if applicable, equipment inspected and certified before use

identification_signs: Mud or sediment in working areas

immediate_actions.action: Activate flood alarm and radio emergency channel
All personnel evacuate to higher ground within mine
Activate emergency pumping systems
Assess water source and inflow rate
Seal off affected area if possible using pre-installed bulkheads
Headcount all personnel at assembly points
Notify regulatory agencies and coordinate external dewatering assistance

prevention_measures.geological_surveys: Comprehensive hydrogeological study before mining, regular geological updates during operations
prevention_measures.water_detection: Pre-mining drilling and geophysical surveys to identify water-bearing structures
prevention_measures.barrier_pillars: Adequate barrier pillars between mine workings and surface water bodies per MSHA 30 CFR 75.1700
prevention_measures.pumping_capacity: Redundant pumping systems rated at 200% of maximum anticipated inflow
prevention_measures.monitoring: Continuous water level monitoring in all sumps and outside water bodies

evacuation_routes.vertical_escape: Raise boring or escape shafts to surface
evacuation_routes.horizontal_escape: Main entryways maintained above floor level with walkways
evacuation_routes.floating_egress: Emergency flotation devices pre-positioned in areas prone to flooding

post_incident_procedures.dewatering: Systematic dewatering with continuous structural monitoring
post_incident_procedures.stability_assessment: Geotechnical assessment of mine openings after water recession
post_incident_procedures.electrical_safety: All electrical equipment tested before re-energization
post_incident_procedures.environmental_monitoring: Water quality testing before discharge to environment

identification_signs: Coal or rock outburst sounds (popping, cracking)
Changes in roof bolt torque readings

immediate_actions.action: Sound emergency alarm and evacuate affected area immediately
All personnel withdraw to last known safe location
Conduct headcount and account for all personnel
Do NOT re-enter area to recover equipment or personnel until deemed safe
Initiate search and rescue operations if personnel are trapped
immediate_actions.responsible: Mine rescue team with ground monitoring equipment

immediate_actions.action: Establish exclusion zone and continuous ground monitoring

ground_control_plan_requirements.MSHA_compliance: Per 30 CFR Part 75 Subpart L - Ground Control
ground_control_plan_requirements.roof_bolt_installation: Per approved roof control plan, verified by MSHA inspector
ground_control_plan_requirements.convergence_monitoring: Daily readings in designated stations, immediate reporting of significant changes
ground_control_plan_requirements.supplemental_support: Steel sets, cribs, or shotcrete in weak ground areas
ground_control_plan_requirements.scaling: Regular scaling of loose material from roof and ribs

rescue_operations.trapped_miner_response: Communication attempt via through-earth system, locate trapped miner using listening devices
rescue_operations.stabilization: Stabilize area around collapse zone before entry
rescue_operations.extrication: Careful removal of material with continuous ground monitoring
rescue_operations.medical_standby: EMS staged at mine portal during rescue operations

methane_CH4.sources: Coal seams, adjacent abandoned workings, gas-bearing formations

action_levels.5_percent: Full evacuation, no electrical equipment operation

carbon_dioxide_CO2.sources: Decomposing organic material, certain geological formations, combustion processes
carbon_dioxide_CO2.detection: CO2 sensors in return air and dead-end headings

hydrogen_sulfide_H2S.danger_level: Extremely toxic, IDLH at 100 ppm, odor of rotten eggs at low concentrations but paralyzes olfactory nerve at dangerous levels
hydrogen_sulfide_H2S.sources: Certain geological formations, decomposing organic material, mine water
hydrogen_sulfide_H2S.detection: Dedicated H2S monitors at all working faces

carbon_monoxide_CO.danger_level: Toxic, prevents oxygen transport in blood, IDLH at 1200 ppm
carbon_monoxide_CO.sources: Fire, diesel exhaust, blasting fumes, oxidation processes
carbon_monoxide_CO.detection: CO monitors, personal monitors on all underground workers

immediate_actions.action: Don self-rescuer immediately upon gas alarm activation
Sound gas alarm and evacuate via fresh air base to surface
immediate_actions.responsible: First person to detect or alarm activation

immediate_actions.action: Activate ventilation emergency procedures (increase air quantity or adjust fans)
De-energize electrical equipment in affected zone if methane is detected
Headcount and account for all personnel
Atmospheric monitoring from safe location to determine extent and concentration
Determine source of gas and implement control measures

ventilation_emergency_procedures.fan_failure: Activate standby fan within 15 minutes, evacuate underground if ventilation cannot be restored, monitor methane levels continuously
ventilation_emergency_procedures.reversal: Controlled reversal only with mine manager approval, notify all underground personnel before action
ventilation_emergency_procedures.boosting: Portable fans deployed to maintain minimum airflow in critical areas

identification_signs: Visible flame or smoke from surface structures
Fire alarm activation in plants or buildings

immediate_actions.action: Call 911 and activate facility fire alarm
Evacuate all personnel from affected building or area
Attempt suppression with portable extinguishers if safe to do so and fire is small
Shut down affected equipment and close fuel shutoff valves
Establish fire perimeter and keep clear for emergency services access
Account for all personnel at assembly points
Provide fire department with site plans, hazardous material inventories, and access information

wildfire_response.defensible_space: Maintain 100-foot defensible space around all surface structures
wildfire_response.evacuation_triggers: Wind-driven fire within 1 mile, air quality index above 300
wildfire_response.coordination: Work with local fire agencies, provide heavy equipment for firebreak construction

classification.minor: Contained within secondary containment, no exposure risk, less than 10 gallons
classification.moderate: Partial containment breach, potential exposure, 10-100 gallons
classification.major: Complete containment failure, actual exposure, greater than 100 gallons
classification.catastrophic: Environmental release, water contamination, mass exposure

immediate_actions.action: Alert personnel in area and establish exclusion zone upwind and uphill
Identify chemical from SDS (Safety Data Sheet) and assess hazards
Don appropriate PPE before attempting containment
Stop source of release if safe to do so (close valves, plug leaks)
Contain spill using booms, berms, absorbent materials
Notify environmental department and safety department
Report to regulatory agencies if reportable quantity released

sodium_cyanide.hazard: Extremely toxic, releases HCN gas when acidic
sodium_cyanide.PPE: Full face respirator with cyanide-specific cartridge, chemical suit, neoprene gloves
sodium_cyanide.neutralization: Sodium hypochlorite solution, alkaline pH above 10

sulfuric_acid.hazard: Corrosive, releases toxic SO2 gas when heated
sulfuric_acid.PPE: Full face respirator, acid-resistant suit, face shield
sulfuric_acid.reporting: Report release exceeding RQ of 1000 lbs

sodium_hydroxide.PPE: Chemical splash goggles, face shield, chemical-resistant clothing
sodium_hydroxide.neutralization: Dilute acid or citric acid solution

diesel_fuel.PPE: Vapor-supplying respirator in confined spaces, chemical suit
diesel_fuel.containment: Absorbent booms and pads, dike with soil
diesel_fuel.reporting: State environmental agency if impact to waterway

froth_reagents.PPE: Per SDS requirements, typically chemical goggles and gloves
froth_reagents.containment: Absorbent materials, prevent entry to drains

severity_levels.level_1: Contained spill within secondary containment, no personnel exposure
severity_levels.level_2: Uncontained spill, potential personnel exposure, no water body impact
severity_levels.level_3: Release to environment or water body, actual or potential human exposure
severity_levels.level_4: Massive release, multiple exposures, water supply contamination

immediate_actions.action: Evacuate all personnel from spill area immediately - cyanide is instantly lethal at high concentrations
Activate cyanide emergency alarm and notify all mine personnel
Shut off cyanide supply pumps and close isolation valves
Establish upwind exclusion zone (minimum 500 meters for large spills)
Deploy emergency cyanide neutralization equipment (hydrogen peroxide, Caro's acid, or alkaline chlorination)
Monitor for HCN gas using dedicated cyanide monitors, establish downwind monitoring stations
Notify downstream water users and environmental agencies immediately
Administer cyanide antidote kit (Cyanokit - hydroxocobalamin) to any exposed persons - call poison control: 1-800-222-1222
Air monitoring for HCN gas before any re-entry - must be below 10 ppm

neutralization_methods.alkaline_chlorination: Raise pH above 10.5, add sodium hypochlorite to oxidize cyanide to cyanate then to CO2 and N2
neutralization_methods.hydrogen_peroxide: Add H2O2 under alkaline conditions to destroy cyanide, effective for large volumes
neutralization_methods.caros_acid: Peroxymonosulfuric acid, rapid destruction of cyanide, requires careful pH control
neutralization_methods.soils_contamination: Excavate contaminated soils, treat on-site or transport to licensed facility
neutralization_methods.water_contamination: Deploy turbidity curtains, pump and treat, activated carbon adsorption

medical_response_cyanide.symptoms: Rapid breathing, headache, dizziness, confusion, seizures, cardiac arrest
medical_response_cyanide.first_aid: Fresh air, 100% oxygen if available, Cyanokit (hydroxocobalamin) 5g IV, amyl nitrite if Cyanokit unavailable
medical_response_cyanide.transport: Immediate ALS transport to nearest hospital with cyanide treatment capability
medical_response_cyanide.decontamination: Remove contaminated clothing, wash skin with copious water

categories.misfire: Failure of explosive charge to detonate
categories.premature_detonation: Unintended detonation during handling or loading
categories.unexploded_ordnance: Unexploded charges in face or muck pile
categories.storage_breach: Unauthorized access or damage to explosives magazine

immediate_actions.action: All personnel evacuate blast zone to safe distance (minimum 500 feet for surface, full evacuation for underground)
Sound explosives alarm (continuous siren)
Establish security perimeter, prevent re-entry
Contact explosives manufacturer technical representative for misfire/hangfire guidance
Do NOT approach misfire or hangfire for minimum 30 minutes (per MSHA 30 CFR 75.1313)
Notify mine manager, safety department, and MSHA if required
Investigate cause and develop remediation plan before any re-entry

misfire_procedures.wait_time: Minimum 30 minutes per MSHA 30 CFR 75.1313 for electric blasting, 60 minutes for non-electric
misfire_procedures.investigation: Blast crew leader, safety representative, and MSHA inspector review circumstances
misfire_procedures.disposition: Re-detonate with fresh primer if accessible, or drill and shoot new hole adjacent to misfire
misfire_procedures.documentation: Complete misfire report including hole location, charge details, circuit integrity

magazine_safety.requirements: Per ATF 27 CFR Part 55 and MSHA 30 CFR 75.1312
magazine_safety.inspections: Daily visual, weekly detailed, annual inventory reconciliation
magazine_safety.separation_distances: Per ATF tables based on quantity of explosives
magazine_safety.protection: Lightning protection, intrusion detection, fire suppression

immediate_actions.action: Secure scene, activate hazard lights on all vehicles
Call emergency medical services, provide GPS coordinates of incident location
Administer first aid if trained, do not move seriously injured persons unless imminent danger
Notify mine dispatch and shift supervisor
Establish traffic control to prevent secondary collisions
Photograph scene before moving vehicles (unless medical emergency)
Drug and alcohol testing per company policy and MSHA requirements

haul_road_emergency.berm_requirements: Per MSHA 30 CFR 56/57.9300 - berms or equivalent protection on haul road edges
haul_road_emergency.signage: Speed limits, grade warnings, blind corner mirrors, intersection warnings
haul_road_emergency.communication: Two-way radio communication between all mobile equipment operators

types: Entanglement in conveyor rollers or pulleys

immediate_actions.action: Emergency stop conveyor using pull cord or emergency stop button
Do NOT attempt to free entangled person while belt is moving
Isolate conveyor electrically - lockout/tagout per MSHA 30 CFR 56/57.14107
Administer first aid once conveyor is de-energized and secured
Call for medical evacuation if required
Preserve scene for investigation, do not restart conveyor until cleared by safety

prevention.safety_devices: Pull cord switches every 50 feet on both sides, zero speed switches, belt alignment switches
prevention.guarding: All moving parts guarded per MSHA 30 CFR 56.14100-14107
prevention.training: Annual conveyor safety training including emergency stop procedures
prevention.lockout_tagout: Complete energy isolation before any maintenance work

hazards.high_voltage: Primary power systems 4.16kV to 69kV, lethal at any contact
hazards.low_voltage: Utilization systems below 600V, still capable of causing cardiac arrest
hazards.static_electrical: Static buildup in dry conditions, ignition source for flammable atmospheres

immediate_actions.action: DO NOT touch victim if still in contact with electrical source
De-energize electrical circuit at nearest disconnect or by calling power dispatch
Verify de-energized state with voltage tester before approaching victim
Move victim from contact point using non-conductive rescue hook or dry rope
Begin CPR/AED immediately if victim is unresponsive and not breathing normally
Call for ALS medical transport, electrical burns require specialized treatment
Secure electrical area and do not re-energize until investigation complete

electrical_safety_program.requirements: Per MSHA 30 CFR Part 56/57 Subpart K
electrical_safety_program.qualified_persons: Only qualified persons may work on energized equipment above 50 volts
electrical_safety_program.ppe: Rubber insulating gloves rated for voltage level, arc flash protection per NFPA 70E
electrical_safety_program.training: Annual electrical safety training including CPR/AED certification

categories.fuel_spill: Diesel, gasoline, hydraulic fluid release to ground or water
categories.process_chemical: Flotation reagents, leach solutions, process water with elevated metals
categories.tailings_release: Tailings dam overtopping or structural failure
categories.seepage: Acid mine drainage or process water seepage to groundwater

immediate_actions.action: Contain spill at source using available materials (soil, absorbent, berms)
Prevent entry to surface water, storm drains, or groundwater
Notify environmental department and document with photographs
Report to state environmental agency and EPA if required (CERCLA/EPCRA thresholds)
immediate_actions.time: Per regulatory requirements (15 minutes to 24 hours depending on severity)

immediate_actions.action: Begin recovery operations using vacuum trucks, booms, skimmers
Conduct environmental assessment of affected area

reporting_thresholds.CERCLA: Release of reportable quantity (RQ) of hazardous substance
reporting_thresholds.EPCRA: Section 304 immediate notification for extremely hazardous substances
reporting_thresholds.Clean_Water_Act: Discharge of pollutants to waters of the United States
reporting_thresholds.RCRA: Hazardous waste release or potential release

underground_communication.primary: Leaky feeder radio system - all underground personnel carry receivers
underground_communication.secondary: Mine telephone system - hard-wired to surface dispatch
underground_communication.tertiary: Through-earth communication system (TEMS) - for emergency rescue
underground_communication.emergency_siren: Three long blasts = evacuate, one long blast = all clear, continuous = emergency

surface_communication.primary: Two-way radio on designated emergency channels
surface_communication.secondary: PA system in all buildings and process areas
surface_communication.tertiary: Cellular phones and satellite phones for remote areas
surface_communication.visual: Strobe lights and rotating beacons at assembly points

alarm_activation_points.pull_stations: Located at every underground section change, at all building exits, at all main access points
alarm_activation_points.manual_call_boxes: At all emergency refuge chambers, at main portal, at all shaft stations
alarm_activation_points.automatic_detection: Fire detection systems, gas monitoring systems, water level monitoring, ground monitoring systems

examples: EMERGENCY - FIRE - MAIN BELT HEAD UG-07 - LEVEL 2 - 3 PERSONNEL INJURED - EVACUATING SECTION - NEED FIRE RESPONSE - J. SMITH SUPERVISOR
EMERGENCY - GROUND FAILURE - DEVELOPMENT HEADING UG-12 - LEVEL 3 - PERSONNEL TRAPPED - RESCUE TEAM DEPLOYED - REQUESTING ADDITIONAL RESCUE - S. JONES SHIFT SUP
initial_message_format.clarity_requirements: Speak slowly and clearly, repeat critical information, confirm receipt of message

fire_department.capabilities: Fire suppression, hazmat response, technical rescue
fire_department.pre_arrangements: Annual site tour, familiarization with mine layout, MSHA training for mutual aid responders

ems.medevac: Helicopter medevac for critical patients, LZ designated on mine property

law_enforcement.capabilities: Scene security, traffic control, criminal investigation

level_1_trauma.name: Regional Medical Center
level_1_trauma.drive_time: 45 minutes by road, 15 minutes by air
level_1_trauma.capabilities: Level 1 Trauma Center, burn unit, toxicology

MSHA.name: Mine Safety and Health Administration
MSHA.reporting_requirement: Fatal accidents within 15 minutes, serious injuries within 15 minutes, all others within 10 working days

support_services.insurance: Workers Compensation Carrier - [Phone Number], Property/Casualty Carrier - [Phone Number]

media_communication.spokesperson_authority: Only designated spokesperson may communicate with media. All media inquiries directed to communications department.

holding_statements.initial: An incident has occurred at [Mine Name]. Emergency response is underway. We are working closely with regulatory agencies. Additional information will be provided as it becomes available.
holding_statements.fatality: We are deeply saddened to confirm a fatality at [Mine Name]. Our thoughts are with the family and coworkers. We are cooperating fully with MSHA and all relevant authorities.
holding_statements.ongoing_response: Emergency response operations continue at [Mine Name]. The situation is [stable/evolving]. [Number] personnel have been accounted for. We will provide updates at [time] intervals.

prohibited_disclosures: Names of victims before family notification
Details that could compromise ongoing rescue operations
Information that could be used in litigation against the company
media_communication.media_staging_area: Designated location away from emergency operations with adequate parking, restroom facilities, and power

family_liaison.activation: Immediately upon any fatality or serious injury requiring hospitalization

liaison_team.support: HR manager, chaplain, trained peer supporters
liaison_team.counseling: Professional grief counselors on-site within 2 hours

notification_procedures.in_person: For fatalities - two-person team visits family in person
notification_procedures.phone: For serious injuries - phone notification followed by in-person visit
notification_procedures.information_provided: Nature of incident, current status, hospital location if applicable, designated contact person for ongoing updates
notification_procedures.ongoing_support: Regular updates every 2 hours during active incident, then daily during recovery period

family_liaison.family_assembly_point: Designated area away from media with private space, refreshments, counseling services, children's care

underground.contents: Burn treatment, eye wash, trauma dressings, splints, tourniquets, emergency blankets
Full trauma kit with hemorrhage control, airway management
Burn treatment, eye wash, minor wound care
Basic first aid, eye wash, bandages

surface.contents: Complete first aid, AED, emergency medications
Burn treatment, eye wash stations, trauma dressings
Burn treatment, eye wash, chemical spill supplies
Trauma kit, eye wash, burn treatment

first_aid_kit_locations.inspection_schedule: Monthly by first aid officer, quarterly comprehensive audit, after each use complete restocking

requirements.response_time: AED accessible within 3 minutes of any work area
requirements.training: All supervisors CPR/AED certified, minimum 2 AED-trained personnel per shift
requirements.inspection: Weekly visual check, monthly function test, pad expiration tracking
requirements.registration: Registered with county EMS for rapid identification during 911 calls

ground_medevac.procedure: Patient loaded in ambucycle or ATV for transport to portal/staging area, then ambulance to hospital
ground_medevac.access_routes: Pre-designated medevac routes maintained clear at all times, marked on mine maps
ground_medevac.equipment: Stretcher, spinal immobilization, trauma kit at each section
ground_medevac.estimated_times: From deepest underground to surface: 30-60 minutes depending on mine layout

air_medevac.procedure: Helicopter landing zone (LZ) designated on mine property, GPS coordinates provided to dispatch, LZ maintained clear and marked
air_medevac.LZ_requirements: 100-foot diameter cleared area, marked with wind sock, night lighting, hazard markings
air_medevac.activation: Via 911 dispatch or direct call to air ambulance service
air_medevac.capabilities: ALS critical care transport, blood products, ventilator, cardiac monitoring
air_medevac.estimated_times: Response: 15-30 minutes, Transport to Level 1 Trauma: 15-45 minutes depending on distance

underground_to_surface.procedure: Patient packaged in stretcher, transported via mantrip or rail car to portal, transferred to ambulance
underground_to_surface.vertical_extraction: If hoist shaft available, patient transported via shaft in specially designed litter platform
underground_to_surface.communication: Continuous communication between underground rescue team and surface EMS during transport

blood_bank_nearest.name: [Regional Blood Bank]
blood_bank_nearest.blood_types_available: All blood types, O-negative emergency supply
blood_bank_nearest.delivery_time: Emergency delivery within 30 minutes, helicopter delivery for mass casualty
blood_bank_nearest.mass_transfusion_protocol: Activate MTP if 3+ units needed, blood bank notified of trauma activation

cyanide_exposure.availability: On-site cyanide emergency kit, hospital pharmacy
cyanide_exposure.protocol: Immediate 100% O2, Cyanokit administration, transport to hospital with toxicology capability

crush_injury.protocol: Aggressive IV fluids before extrication, monitor for hyperkalemia, sodium bicarbonate for acidosis
crush_injury.considerations: Prolonged entrapment may require amputation for rescue

hypothermia.protocol: Remove from cold environment, passive rewarming for mild, active rewarming for moderate/severe
hypothermia.mine_specific: Underground flooding events may result in cold water immersion

triggers: Any order from mine management or MSHA inspector

evacuation_methods.primary: Travel via designated escapeways to surface, using self-rescuer if atmosphere compromised
evacuation_methods.secondary: Via refuge chamber if primary escapeway blocked - activate refuge chamber, communicate with surface, await rescue
evacuation_methods.vertical: Via shaft or raise boring if accessible and safe
evacuation_methods.beltway: Travel on walkway beside conveyor belt - NEVER ride on belt during evacuation

evacuation_speed.normal_conditions: Walk at steady pace, do not run
evacuation_speed.smoke_conditions: Stay low, use self-rescuer, follow luminous markers
evacuation_speed.water_conditions: Move to higher ground immediately, avoid flooded areas
evacuation_speed.complete_darkness: Follow guide rope if available, feel for wall-mounted markers

critical_stations.fresh_air_base: Located at each section, provides communication to surface and fresh air supply
critical_stations.refuge_chamber: Within 1500 feet of all working faces, rated for 96 hours, provides air, water, communication
critical_stations.secondary_escape: Independent ventilation split providing alternative route to surface
critical_stations.emergency_stockpiles: Self-rescuers, first aid, water, and communication devices at strategic locations

zone_A_process_plant.assembly_point: Upper parking lot - 300 meters from process plant
zone_A_process_plant.accountability: Process supervisor conducts headcount at assembly point

zone_C_office_complex.assembly_point: North parking lot - 150 meters from office

zone_D_fuel_storage.assembly_point: East field - 400 meters from fuel farm

zone_E_tailings.assembly_point: West ridge - 500 meters from tailings dam

designated_areas_for_contractors.contractor_assembly: Separate section within primary assembly point with contractor company identification boards
designated_areas_for_contractors.visitor_assembly: Visitors escorted to main assembly point, registered at security gate
designated_areas_for_contractors.headcount_verification: Contractor companies responsible for own headcount, reported to mine safety within 15 minutes of evacuation

underground.method: Electronic tracking system (tag-in/tag-out at portal and section changes), supplemented by supervisor verbal headcount
underground.verification: Section supervisors report to surface dispatch within 10 minutes of alarm
underground.reconciliation: Surface dispatch reconciles tracking system data with shift roster and section reports
underground.incomplete_headcount: Immediately notify mine rescue team, begin search operations

surface.method: Supervisor conducts physical headcount at assembly point
surface.verification: Assembly point marshals report to emergency coordinator within 15 minutes
surface.technology: RFID badges scanned at assembly point readers, automated reconciliation
surface.absentee_accounting: Shift roster cross-referenced with time clock data and visitor logs

visitor_contractors.pre_entry: All visitors and contractors sign in at security gate, issued temporary ID badge with RFID
visitor_contractors.escort_required: Visitors must be escorted at all times while on mine property
visitor_contractors.evacuation_escort: During evacuation, escorts responsible for guiding visitors to assembly point
visitor_contractors.contractor_headcount: Contractor company foreman responsible for own crew headcount, reports to mine safety

pre_arrival.safety_induction: All visitors and contractors must complete mine safety orientation before entry
pre_arrival.documentation: Valid identification, company credentials, medical clearance if required
pre_arrival.insurance: Proof of workers compensation and liability insurance for contractors

on_site.sign_in_out: Mandatory sign-in at security gate with expected departure time
on_site.badge_system: Color-coded badges indicating authorized areas and escort requirements
on_site.escort_requirements: Visitors always escorted, contractors may self-navigate in authorized areas if oriented

evacuation.responsibility: Mine escort or contractor supervisor responsible for visitor/contractor evacuation
evacuation.assembly: Report to designated contractor assembly area, headcount reported to mine safety
evacuation.accountability: No visitor or contractor cleared until accounted for in headcount reconciliation

fire_drill.underground: Monthly - unannounced, different section each time
fire_drill.full_mine: Quarterly - coordinated surface and underground evacuation drill

emergency_response_drill.tabletop: Monthly - different emergency scenario each session
emergency_response_drill.full_scale: Annually - complete emergency response activation with external agencies

evacuation_timing_drills.underground_to_surface: Monthly - timed evacuation drills, target: full evacuation within 30 minutes

drill_types.description: Random activation of fire alarm system with full evacuation procedures
drill_types.success_criteria: 100% evacuation within target time, all headcounts complete within 15 minutes, all self-rescuers donned correctly

drill_types.description: Management team works through emergency scenarios in conference room setting
drill_types.participants: Mine management, safety team, department heads, external agency representatives

drill_types.description: Test specific emergency response systems without full-scale deployment
examples: Communication system test - message from deepest underground to surface within 5 minutes
Emergency lighting system test - all underground lights off, verify backup lighting
Pumping system failure drill - verify backup pumps activate within 15 minutes
AED deployment drill - from storage to patient in under 3 minutes
Cyanide neutralization drill - deploy neutralization equipment within 15 minutes

drill_types.description: Complete activation of emergency response system with external agency participation
drill_types.participants: All mine personnel, local fire department, EMS, MSHA (invited), hospital
drill_types.scenario: Complex multi-hazard event requiring coordinated response
drill_types.success_criteria: All notification chains completed, all response teams deployed within target times, medical transport initiated within 30 minutes, media response activated

drill_types.description: Mine rescue teams practice in simulated mine rescue scenarios
drill_types.participants: Certified mine rescue teams (4-person teams minimum)

drill_types.description: All underground personnel practice self-rescuer donning in simulated emergency conditions
drill_types.success_criteria: Self-rescuer donned correctly within 60 seconds, proper seal check completed, all personnel participate

completion.personnel_accounted_for: 100% of on-site personnel must be accounted for
completion.equipment_deployment: All required emergency equipment deployed and functional
completion.documentation: Complete drill record with timing, observations, deficiencies

effectiveness.decision_making: Timely and appropriate decisions by incident command
effectiveness.resource_allocation: Adequate resources deployed to appropriate locations
effectiveness.coordination: Effective coordination between all response teams
effectiveness.safety: No safety issues during drill execution

deficiency_documentation.immediate_correction: Any safety-related deficiency corrected immediately during drill
deficiency_documentation.short_term_correction: Procedural or equipment deficiencies corrected within 30 days
deficiency_documentation.long_term_correction: Systemic or infrastructure deficiencies corrected within 90 days with project plan

corrective_action_process.identification: Drill after-action report identifies all deficiencies
corrective_action_process.assignment: Each deficiency assigned to responsible person with completion deadline
corrective_action_process.tracking: Maintained in corrective action tracking system with status updates
corrective_action_process.verification: Completed corrective actions verified by safety department
corrective_action_process.closure: Formal closure with documentation after verification

continuous_improvement.lessons_learned: Lessons from each drill shared with all personnel via safety meetings
continuous_improvement.procedure_updates: Emergency procedures updated based on drill findings within 30 days
continuous_improvement.training_updates: Training program modified to address identified weaknesses
continuous_improvement.annual_review: Comprehensive review of all emergency procedures annually incorporating drill results
continuous_improvement.benchmarking: Compare response times and procedures against industry best practices and MSHA guidelines

record_keeping.drill_records: Maintained for minimum 5 years, include timing data, participant lists, observer notes
record_keeping.after_action_reports: Completed within 72 hours of each drill
record_keeping.trend_analysis: Annual analysis of drill performance trends to identify systemic issues

Part_46.title: Training and Retraining of Miners
key_requirements: New miner training - minimum 40 hours (underground) or 24 hours (surface)
New task training before performing new tasks
Emergency procedures training included in all training programs
Self-rescuer training and practice - quarterly for underground

Part_48.title: Training and Retraining of Miners (Alternates)
key_requirements: Emergency response training for all miners
Mine rescue team training per Part 46
First aid training for designated first aid providers
Fire training for all underground personnel

Part_77.title: Surface Coal Mines and Surface Work Areas of Underground Coal Mines

written_reports_to_MSHA.Form_7000_1: Within 10 working days of accident or injury
written_reports_to_MSHA.root_cause_analysis: Required for serious accidents as determined by MSHA

state_requirements.note: Additional reporting requirements per state mining safety regulations - consult state agency for specific requirements
state_requirements.typical_requirements: Similar to federal, some states require faster notification and more detailed reporting

environmental_reporting.CERCLA: Release of reportable quantity within 15 minutes to National Response Center
environmental_reporting.EPCRA: Section 304 immediate notification for extremely hazardous substances
environmental_reporting.Clean_Water_Act: NPDES permit violations reported per permit conditions
environmental_reporting.RCRA: Hazardous waste incidents reported within 24 hours

MSHA_inspection_readiness.documentation: All emergency procedures documented, accessible, and current
MSHA_inspection_readiness.training_records: All personnel training records up to date and readily available
MSHA_inspection_readiness.drill_records: Complete drill records with after-action reports available
MSHA_inspection_readiness.equipment_records: All emergency equipment inspection and maintenance records current
MSHA_inspection_readiness.mine_maps: Current mine maps showing all emergency features, escape ways, refuge chambers

inspection_response.accompany_inspector: Safety manager or designee accompanies MSHA inspector
inspection_response.correct_violations: Serious violations corrected immediately, others per abatement schedule
inspection_response.appeal_rights: Understanding of contest rights and procedures for citations

BG4_breathing_apparatus.inspection: Monthly functional test, annual hydrostatic test

self_rescuers.location: Within 25 feet of all working positions

gas_detections.calibration: Weekly bump test, monthly full calibration

through_earth_system.capability: Surface to underground through 1000 feet of rock

emergency_phones.location: Every section, refuge chambers, main entries

spill_response_carts.location: Fuel storage, chemical storage, process areas

summer.heat_stress: Modified work schedules, mandatory hydration, cooling stations, additional medical monitoring
summer.wildfire: Heightened monitoring, evacuation plans updated, defensible space maintained
summer.flooding: Monsoon season monitoring, pump capacity verification, weather alert system

winter.cold_stress: Warm-up shelters, frostbite prevention training, modified schedules for extreme cold
winter.ice: Road maintenance, anti-icing operations, vehicle safety checks
winter.short_days: Extended lighting requirements, visibility measures on haul roads

multi_shift_operations.shift_changes: Overlap period of 15 minutes between shifts to ensure continuity of emergency readiness
multi_shift_operations.shift_supervisors: Each shift has designated emergency coordinator and backup
multi_shift_operations.communication_handoff: Briefing between shifts includes current emergency status and any active incidents

contractor_management.pre_qualification: Contractors must demonstrate emergency response capability before award
contractor_management.site_specific: Contractors receive site-specific emergency procedures orientation
contractor_management.integration: Contractor emergency plans integrated with mine emergency plans
contractor_management.accountability: Contractor foremen responsible for crew safety and headcount during emergencies

public_communities.community_notification: Mutual aid agreements with neighboring communities, community warning systems for mine emergencies
public_communities.air_quality: Community air monitoring during fire or dust events, public notification of exceedances
public_communities.water_quality: Downstream water quality monitoring, community notification of releases
